T: Pines, crowding close. The camp likes it that way.
M: The hill's rock face. An old fort is buried in it, wall and all.
Higher up, a rusted horn juts from the rock. At dusk it plays four cheerful notes.
The deserters hum along. They hate that they hum along.
E: The fort's arch, half swallowed by the hill. Cold air breathes out of it.
Carved above, half gone: "…LECREST SECOND REGIMENT…"
A: A tent, more patch than tent. A plank by the flap reads NOT A DESERTERS' CAMP.
x: A campfire. Someone's roasting something that might once have been a turnip.
O: A boulder, wedged into a gap in the rock face. There's a space behind it.
Too heavy to move. It would take real strength to shift it.
Y: A child's wooden sword, worn smooth where a small hand held it.
Z: A statue of a king in robes, snapped off at the neck. The plaque has been pried off.
Somebody has planted roses all round it anyway, and keeps them very well.
(The Mad King. Out here, somebody still kneels for him.)
6: Roses, red and white, weeded to the last leaf.
Not one of them is facing the Kingdom.
J: A cocoon, tucked in between the tents and the trees.
Someone has wrapped an old soldier's scarf round the silk, to keep it warm.

objects.name: Old Fen
lines: Mess hall's haunted. Armoury's haunted. The drill yard's haunted by something that shouts. The rest is fine.

answer: Rooms, holes, ladders. More holes than a courier's socks.
Only one hole goes anywhere. The others go somewhere worse.
Behind that boulder in the rock, there's a gap. Found a child's toy sword in there once. Put it back.
Didn't feel like mine to take.
Doesn't stop me walking. Just stops me walking fast.
The old riddle round this fire: why would a shadow make a king?
Some say to rule. Some say to stop the war. I say don't ask it after dark.

questions.ask: You smell worse than the haunted mess.
answer: That's not me. That's the mess.

objects.name: Old Mags
lines: Hm? Oh. A visitor. Mind the roses, dear. They're his.
My great-grandmother used to tell me a tale, when I was small.
A prince. Who got lost in the woods.
Deities, toying with the King's mind. He never stood a chance.
I wonder if the prince is still out there.
They never found him, you know.
* She turns back to the statue, and pats its plinth, the way you'd pat an old friend's knee.
Don't mind me. Just the ramblings of an old person.
Under a tent peg marked NOT A TREASURE: a Heart Piece.
The deserters are very consistent about their signs.

objects.name: The Traveler
lines: Oh! Hello, hello! Lovely day for it.

objects.name: Iris
lines: Oh. Morning. Is it morning? I slept. I actually slept.
I was a soldier, once. I remember the drums. I remember deciding I'd had enough of them.
Some days are heavy. I carry them, and set them down at night. I think I'll set this one down at the Archive.
* Iris winds her scarf twice round, and walks off toward the Archive, slowly, like someone with nowhere she has to be.
